title: bpm.api_tenant_context uses threadlocal storage; worker threads spawned mid-test don't inherit the spawning thread's tenant context, causing pool.acquire() to fall back to search_path=public
summary: Discovered while implementing and verifying the ISS-0095 fix (GitHub #349). tests/integration/instance_error_test.zig's TC-EE-10-05 spawns two std.Thread.spawn worker threads, each of which calls pool.acquire() independently. src/api/tenant_context.zig stores the current tenant id in a `threadlocal var`, so a .set() call made on the spawning/main thread (whether inside makePool() per the ISS-0095 fix, or inside TestHarness.init()) is invisible to the worker threads' own thread-local storage. Each worker thread's pool.acquire() therefore sees no tenant context set on ITS thread and falls back to search_path=public, where the business tables the worker needs no longer exist post-GBL-073. This is architecturally distinct from ISS-0095 (which was about a missing .set() call on the calling thread entirely) -- it cannot be fixed by editing makePool(), since makePool() already runs (and now correctly sets context) on the main thread before any worker thread is spawned.

root_cause.details: src/api/tenant_context.zig's tenant-id storage is declared as a Zig `threadlocal var`. Any std.Thread.spawn()'d worker thread starts with its own zero-initialized copy of that threadlocal storage, regardless of what the parent thread had set. TC-EE-10-05 in tests/integration/instance_error_test.zig relies on both worker threads sharing the same tenant-scoped pool connections as the main test thread, but each worker's first pool.acquire() call resolves tenant context independently and gets the threadlocal's zero-value (empty/unset), triggering pool.zig's documented empty-context-means-public fallback.

files_to_change: Needs a design decision before implementation: options include (a) passing an explicit tenant-id parameter into worker thread entry functions and having them call api_tenant_context.set() as their first statement, (b) a pool-level API that accepts an explicit tenant id per-acquire rather than relying on ambient threadlocal state, or (c) restructuring tenant_context storage to not be threadlocal (would need concurrency-safety review, since the whole point of threadlocal here appears to be avoiding cross-request tenant leakage in a multi-threaded server). Affected test: tests/integration/instance_error_test.zig (TC-EE-10-05). Possible production-code implication: any production code path that spawns worker threads and expects them to inherit request-scoped tenant context would have the same gap -- worth a broader grep for std.Thread.spawn usage in src/ as part of the eventual fix's investigation, not assumed here.

occurrences.context: Found by BACKEND-DEV while implementing the ISS-0095 fix. Confirmed pre-existing via git stash: the pre-fix baseline fails this same test even earlier (at def_store.create(), before the worker threads are even spawned), so this is not a regression introduced by the ISS-0095 fix -- the fix gets the test further along (past the main-thread setup) but does not reach a passing state due to this separate gap.

prevention: When adding new tests that spawn worker threads and touch tenant-scoped resources, explicitly document and test the thread's own tenant-context setup rather than assuming it inherits from the spawning thread.

Consider whether any production request-handling code path spawns worker threads for tenant-scoped work -- if so, this could be a production-severity gap, not just a test-environment one; needs investigation as part of the eventual fix, not assumed here since this issue was discovered via a test file, not a production code audit.
